{"retrieved_sources": {"BRD-K08109215": [{"source_id": "pubchem:46943432:description:1", "text": "Molibresib is a member of the class of triazolobenzodiazepine that is 4H-[1,2,4]triazolo[4,3-a][1,4]benzodiazepine substituted by methyl, 2-(ethylamino)-2-oxoethyl, 4-chlorophenyl, and methoxy groups at positions 1, 4S, 6, and 8, respectively. It is an orally bioavailable inhibitor of BET family of proteins that has demonstrated antitumour activity in preclinical models of solid and hematologic malignancies. It has a role as a bromodomain-containing protein 4 inhibitor, an antineoplastic agent and an apoptosis inducer. It is a secondary carboxamide, a triazolobenzodiazepine, an aromatic ether and a member of monochlorobenzenes.", "provider": null, "url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=CHEBI:95082"}], "BRD-K83189926": [{"source_id": "pubchem:57339144:description:1", "text": "[3-anilino-4-[oxo-[4-(1-pyrrolidinyl)-1-piperidinyl]methyl]phenyl]-[4-(1-pyrrolidinyl)-1-piperidinyl]methanone is a member of benzamides and a N-acylpiperidine.", "provider": null, "url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=CHEBI:95086"}], "BRD-K56343971": [{"source_id": "pubchem:42611257:description:1", "text": "Vemurafenib is a pyrrolopyridine that is 1H-pyrrolo[2,3-b]pyridine which is substituted at position 5 by a p-chlorophenyl group and at positions 3 by a 3-amino-2,6-difluorobenzoyl group, the amino group of which has undergone formal condensation with propane-1-sulfonic acid to give the corresponding sulfonamide. An inhibitor of BRAF and other kinases. It has a role as an antineoplastic agent and a B-Raf inhibitor. It is a sulfonamide, a difluorobenzene, a pyrrolopyridine, an aromatic ketone and a member of monochlorobenzenes.", "provider": null, "url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=CHEBI:63637"}], "BRD-K49328571": [{"source_id": "pubchem:3062316:description:1", "text": "Dasatinib (anhydrous) is an aminopyrimidine that is 2-methylpyrimidine which is substituted at position 4 by the primary amino group of 2-amino-1,3-thiazole-5-carboxylic acid and at position 6 by a 4-(2-hydroxyethyl)piperazin-1-yl group, and in which the carboxylic acid group has been formally condensed with 2-chloro-6-methylaniline to afford the corresponding amide. A multi-targeted kinase inhibitor, it is used, particularly as the monohydrate, for the treatment of chronic, accelerated, or myeloid or lymphoid blast phase chronic myeloid leukemia. Note that the name 'dasatinib' is used to refer to the monohydrate (USAN) as well as to anhydrous dasatinib (INN). It has a role as an anticoronaviral agent, an antineoplastic agent and a tyrosine kinase inhibitor. It is a monocarboxylic acid amide, an organochlorine compound, an aminopyrimidine, a member of 1,3-thiazoles, a N-arylpiperazine, a N-(2-hydroxyethyl)piperazine, a secondary amino compound and a tertiary amino compound. donors.reason: BET bromodomain inhibitor like JQ1-S; same target class, best-supported mechanistic match for histone-mark transfer.
Methyl-lysine reader inhibitor; chromatin-reader perturbation may resemble BET inhibition, but source lacks target detail.
BRAF inhibitor; A375 is BRAF-mutant, so kinase-pathway control for histone-mark changes.
Multi-targeted kinase inhibitor; negative-control donor for non-bromodomain kinase effects on histone marks.
DNA methyltransferase inhibitor; high anchor similarity suggests shared downstream histone-mark response despite different target.

revised_hypotheses: GSK525762A (BRD-K08109215) is the strongest mechanistic donor because it is a BET bromodomain inhibitor, matching JQ1-S pharmacology.
UNC1215 (BRD-K83189926) may partially match via chromatin-reader inhibition, but its retrieved source does not confirm a specific reader target.
Vemurafenib and Dasatinib serve as kinase-pathway controls; their low anchor similarity predicts poor histone-mark transfer.
Decitabine may share downstream histone-mark changes with JQ1-S, but its DNA methyltransferase mechanism differs from BET inhibition.
unresolved: No measured histone-mark response values for JQ1-S or donors in A375; transfer reproducibility >0.5 log2 vs vehicle cannot be confirmed.
UNC1215 target specificity is not established from the retrieved source.
Whether anchor similarity reflects shared mechanism or cell-state confounding remains untested.
